connector: No new chapters today. You get to be the detective. Find the exact words Lewis uses for what Lucy feels and hears, and the strange lamp-post glowing in the wood. Those words are your evidence.

a.raw: when lucy reached the lamp-post she heard a pitter patter of feet
a.fixed: When Lucy reached the lamp-post, she heard a pitter patter of feet.
a.why: When starts the part that cannot stand alone. A comma goes after it, before the main idea. Lucy is a name. A period ends it.

b.raw: when lucy was tired of eating the faun began to talk
b.fixed: When Lucy was tired of eating, the Faun began to talk.
b.why: When starts the part that cannot stand alone, so a comma goes after eating. Lucy is a name, and the Faun is used as his name.

cards.title: World Notes: Lamp-Posts and Lamplighters
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapters with your lens in mind.
text: Long ago, before electric lights, many streets in London were lit by gas lamps on tall posts.
Each evening a lamplighter walked from post to post to light them, and each morning he put them out.
A lamp-post on a city street was ordinary. A lamp-post alone in a snowy wood is very strange!

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Detective day! Find the exact words Lewis uses to make Narnia feel real.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build tele words, join two sentences, and find which vowel blurred.
transcripts.guide2: Look back at Chapters 1 to 3 for the exact words you need.
transcripts.guide3: Today you write two evidence sentences with short quotes.

notes.wordParts: The word part tele means far. telephone = sound from far away. telescope = a tool for looking far away.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main idea and a part that cannot stand alone, joined by a word like when, because or although. When that part comes first, put a comma after it.
notes.spelling: The schwa is a lazy uh sound in a quiet beat of a long word. Any vowel can make it: the a in sofa, the e in seven, the o in lemon.
notes.wgrd: Point to the exact words. Lewis tells what Lucy feels and hears: snow that is soft and powdery and extremely cold, and something crunching under her feet.
vocab: eager to find out; very curious
a deep feeling of sadness or gloom
strange or unusual in a hard-to-explain way

mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Detectives point to proof. When you say Narnia feels real, point to Lewis's exact words: what Lucy felt, and what she heard. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. When Lucy stepped through the fur coats, she felt snow under her shoes. When starts the part that can't stand alone. The comma goes right where that part ends. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Say the parts out loud. Type the whole word in each box. Tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: Snap the parts together, like blocks. Tele. Photo. Telephoto! A telephoto lens on a camera takes pictures of things far away. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.

mods.todo: Read each sentence. Pick the word that fits.
mods.script: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. Lucy took a quick blank back at the wardrobe. Spiteful? No. Glimpse? Yes! A glimpse is a quick look. Now pick the word that fits each sentence.

mods.todo: Read the before and after. Join the two sentences in the box.
mods.script: Two short sentences can become one. The others did not believe Lucy. She was very unhappy. Put a joining word in front: Because the others did not believe her, comma, Lucy was very unhappy. Read the before and after. Then join the two sentences in the box.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Lucy could have said the story was made up for fun, but she would not say it.
items.why: Lucy was a very truthful girl, even when it made her unhappy.

items.t: Edmund sneered and jeered, and asked if Lucy had found new countries in other cupboards.
items.why: He was being spiteful, not honest.

items.t: In Narnia, Edmund shouts, “I’m sorry I didn’t believe you. I see now you were right all along.”
items.why: He says out loud that he was wrong.
